test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Raju said to Reghu, “Stay back.

options.text: Raju has ordered Reghu to stay back.
Raju ordered Reghu to stay back.
Raju had ordered Reghu to stay back.
Raju orders Reghu to stay back.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reported Speech:** The given sentence uses direct speech, where the speaker is addressing someone with a request or instruction. When converting to reported speech, it changes to an indirect form, without the quotation marks.
 
• In reported speech, the reporting verb changes according to the nature of the command. In this case, since it's a request or suggestion, the verb should be "ordered".
 
• Option 2 correctly changes the direct speech to reported speech by using the verb "ordered" and keeping the structure intact.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Raju ordered Reghu to stay back."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Raju has ordered Reghu to stay back." – Incorrect because "has ordered" uses the present perfect tense, which is not suitable for reporting a past action in this context.
 
• **Option 3:** "Raju had ordered Reghu to stay back." – Incorrect because it uses past perfect tense, which is not needed here.
 
• **Option 4:** "Raju orders Reghu to stay back." – Incorrect because "orders" is in the present tense, while the reporting verb should match the past tense of the direct speech.
